text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Public Works Minister Abdelaziz Meziane says Morocco hopes that Gibraltar tunnel drilling will start within less than four years. The two-stage tunnel works will cost an estimated $4.9 billion.
- Providing jobs for unemployed university graduates is a sacred national duty. There are between 300,000 and 320,000 job seekers a year and only about 200,000 of them find work.

- Former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker, appointed as U.N secretary-general's personal representative for the Western Sahara conflict, will visit Morocco, Algeria and Mauritania in bid to revive a U.N. peace plan for the territory.
- Morocco seeks a market for its agricultural products in the Gulf Arab states. It will set up a centre for its products in Bahrain.
- Canadian business delegation starts an eight-day visit to Morocco on April 22.
- French firm Lyonnaise des Eaux, which had won a 30-year deal to manage Casablanca power and water network, pledges to keep consumer prices unchanged for 12 months.
- About 130 unemployed doctors ended a hunger strike after winning promise from the authorities to give them jobs within the next few days.
- A forest guard was shot dead in Khenifra.
- The interior ministry carries out "secret" polls to sound out Moroccans ahead of the elections.
